column1: # The std part of `fix --edition rust`'s rewrite table (plan §6, "std
# calls"): for each MVS std item whose call changes, its rust-edition form,
# chosen by type. Read by the translator (0.27.3). Columns, tab-separated:
#   mvs     the MVS item (Owner::name, or a free function's name)
#   when    when the row applies: `-` always; a type condition on the
#           receiver's element or key type (T, K, V, E: `T: Copy`, `T: !Copy`,
#           what the call's value is used for (read and dropped, moved into a
#           place, stored or returned); the first row that applies wins
#   rust    the rust-edition call: $r the receiver, $1 $2 ... the arguments
#           (already rewritten as expressions), $a an allocator argument,
#           `-` for a statement that disappears, `!` for a call the
#           translator reports for a hand fix
# A row whose rust column starts with `type ` rewrites a type's name where
# it is written (its arguments $1 $2 ... as rewritten), one starting with
# `impl ` an impl of the trait: what its items become.
# An MVS item with no row keeps its call as written: the type-directed
# parameter rewrite (`let` to &T, `inout` to &mut T, `&x` at a call from
# the parameter's type) makes its receivers and arguments references.
